items.title: Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1962-08-26
items.q: He had Kidore on trombone, Johnny Dodge on clarinet.

ctx.x: When did you first hear Oliver that you can remember?

Oh, I think it was around 1917 at Tulane Gym. They gave subscription dances every Saturday night at Tulane Gym. And every time they could get him, they got him. Yeah. And they got him for everything else they could get him for too. He had the cream of the crop. He had Kidore on trombone, Johnny Dodge on clarinet. And I don't know whether Baby Dodge was playing drums then. He didn't have Baby Dodge on the drums.
No, I think he used different people like Red Happy, they called him.

items.title: Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1969-12-14
items.q: Ori's Creole Trombone, that record, if you were able to get it

ctx.x: You can just make a list. You can... Yeah, if you make a list, he'll tell you what's what. But you can rely on anything he says.

Uh-huh. She could call me at extension 7604. I think it's very nice that Johnny said such flattering things about my knowledge, especially after I said how much I learned from him. That's funny. That's amazing. I'd like to see just what would be worrisome, because some of them are dated 1908, 1909. Yes. Well, they vary, of course, in value. And these things are sold to collectors all over the world through small magazines, such as Record Research out of Brooklyn, New York. And they'll have a list and auction them…
You know, man, I got that myself.
